doc.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Listening to current artists
summary: She listens less now, focused on television and editing a San Diego big band, but follows Hancock, Silver and Shorter.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Right. Do you listen to current artists coming out these days?

I do. I have to say reluctantly that I listen not as much as I want to. I will be doing more listening, but at the present time I am more looking to produce quality television, and so I focus more on that. I do try to present music. I’m currently editing a big band, it’s a San Diego concert jazz band, I’m currently editing that. And that music is what I hear every day. So I’m sort of a focused person, so the music that’s wonderful today, yes, I try my best to keep up somehow with it. But I get kind of side tracked with television.
Do you still take an interest in the careers of people like Joe Henderson that are still out there?
Sure. Herbie Hancock, Horace Silver, all the guys, Wayne Shorter, sure. I’m very interested and I’m always trusting that they continue for a long time.
